# Pbwire Elixir binding (`bindings/elixir`)

> The Elixir binding of [pbwire](../../README.md): `elixir-protobuf` structs
> through the Erlang NIF (`:pbwire`) over the shared C core. The generated
> `__message_props__/0` is the schema source the way gpb's `get_msg_defs/0`
> is for Erlang; `Pbwire.load_schema/1` consumes it and `Pbwire.encode/1` /
> `decode/2` run in C. Same structs, same wire format, byte-identical
> output to `Protobuf.encode/1`, ~1.4-3.2x faster than pure-Elixir
> elixir-protobuf, with no `FileDescriptorSet` and no second wire
> implementation.

Facts: developed in this repo as `bindings/elixir`, license Apache-2.0 (see
the repo root). Hex package `pbwire_elixir`; the NIF itself ships in the
Erlang `pbwire` package. Requirements: Elixir per
[`.tool-versions`](.tool-versions), a C compiler, `make`, Hex access. `make`
compiles the repo's C core into `build/` here (nothing is written outside
`bindings/elixir/`); `mix` then compiles the `:pbwire` dep against it.

## Build

```shell
make          # from bindings/elixir: core lib + deps + compile
make test     # ExUnit: byte-identity with Protobuf.encode, struct equality with Protobuf.decode
make bench    # four standard tiers vs elixir-protobuf on matrix3.proto
```

## Docs

- [README](README.md): build, quick start, full API reference, supported protobuf features, options, benchmark table, FAQ.
- [benchmarks/bench.exs](benchmarks/bench.exs): byte-gated harness (pinned 136 / 174 / 2469 / 74913 bytes) before timing.
- [conformance/README.md](conformance/README.md): status and plan (blocked on test-message module-name collisions).

## API

- `Pbwire.load_schema([MyApp.Person])` -> `:ok`; loads/replaces the global schema cache (transitive: referenced messages and enums come along). Options `with_utf8: true` (default) and `string_as_list: true` go to `:pbwire.set_opts/1` first.
- `Pbwire.purge_schema()` -> `:ok`; clears the schema.
- `Pbwire.encode(%MyApp.Person{})` -> `binary()`; byte-identical to `Protobuf.encode/1`.
- `Pbwire.decode(bin, MyApp.Person)` -> struct; equal to `Protobuf.decode(bin, MyApp.Person)`.
- `Pbwire.encode_msg(struct, mods)` / `Pbwire.decode_msg(bin, mod, mods)`: load the schema on each call.

Unknown fields are dropped on decode; missing `required` fields raise
instead of filling defaults; `NaN` bit-identity is not preserved (any
NaN bits decode to `:nan`).

## Key facts

- Supports all scalar types, enums (unknown numbers decode to integers), repeated/packed fields, nested messages, oneof (`{member, value}`), maps (Elixir maps), proto3 zero-omission and `proto3_optional` presence. No groups or extensions (`elixir-protobuf` generates neither).
- Struct names in the NIF cache are the Elixir module atoms, so schemas cannot collide the way unqualified record names do.
- The schema cache is global to the BEAM node; encode/decode are concurrency-safe; calls run on normal schedulers.
- `elixir-protobuf` structs are the generated model: there is no `codegen` output for Elixir.

## Optional

- [test/pbwire_test.exs](test/pbwire_test.exs): parity tests against the oracle, useful as executable usage examples.
- [lib/pbwire/schema.ex](lib/pbwire/schema.ex): the generated-module to NIF-defs translator.
